```{python}
#| label: completed-onelead-setup
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from live_results import *

QUEUE_DB = source_path("refine-logs/wavelet_ssl_1110000/full/queue.sqlite")
queue = load_onelead_queue(QUEUE_DB)
completed = queue.query("status == 'completed'").copy()
failed = queue.query("status != 'completed'").copy()
metrics = numeric_metrics(completed, "metric.")
```

## Evidence contract

This chapter freezes the interpretation of the completed three-epoch
`1110000`, seed-42 screening experiment. It is separate from the live queue,
longer convergence extensions, spatial experiments, and external RDB
evaluation. A completed screening row is not a replicated confirmatory result.

The primary registered chain is `A0 raw → A0 + wavelet → A0 + wavelet +
SSL`. E1 is a complementarity test, not an improved baseline. Lead I and lead
II are separate input contracts and are never averaged before showing their
individual results.

## Completion and failure accounting

```{python}
#| label: completed-onelead-accounting
display(source_inventory({"1110000 queue": QUEUE_DB}))
display(queue.groupby(["observed_lead", "status"], dropna=False).size()
        .rename("runs").reset_index())
failure_cols = [c for c in ["ordinal", "id", "cell_name", "observed_lead",
                            "status", "attempts", "error"] if c in failed]
display(failed[failure_cols].sort_values("ordinal"))
```

The denominator remains 120. Failed, interrupted, and out-of-memory cells stay
visible; they are not converted to missing-at-random observations and are not
silently removed from coverage statements.

## Every completed model and every stored numeric metric

```{python}
#| label: completed-onelead-all-metrics
identity = [c for c in ["ordinal", "id", "cell_name", "observed_lead", "seed",
                         "completed_at"] if c in completed]
all_results = completed[identity + metrics].sort_values(["observed_lead", "ordinal"])
display(all_results)
display(pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": metrics,
    "direction": [metric_direction(metric) or "context only" for metric in metrics],
    "nonmissing_rows": [int(completed[metric].notna().sum()) for metric in metrics],
}))
```

The exhaustive table is deliberately database-backed rather than copied to a
CSV. Training-component losses and peak memory are included for diagnosis but
are not interchangeable with held-out endpoints. The boundary metrics carrying
the `_smoke` suffix come from the internal smoke subset, not blinded external
LUDB/RDB evaluation.

## Matched changes from A0

```{python}
#| label: completed-onelead-matched-a0
matched = matched_deltas(completed, BASELINE)
delta_cols = [c for c in matched if c.startswith("improvement.metric.")]
visible = [c for c in ["id", "cell_name", "observed_lead", "seed", *delta_cols]
           if c in matched]
display(matched[visible].sort_values(["observed_lead", "cell_name"]))
if delta_cols:
    heat = matched.groupby(["cell_name", "observed_lead"])[delta_cols].mean().reset_index()
    heat["configuration"] = heat.cell_name + " · Lead " + heat.observed_lead
    fig = px.imshow(heat.set_index("configuration")[delta_cols], aspect="auto",
                    color_continuous_scale="RdBu", color_continuous_midpoint=0,
                    title="Single-seed matched improvement over A0; positive is favorable")
    fig.update_layout(height=max(550, 23 * len(heat)))
    fig.show()
```

## Registered mechanism contrasts

```{python}
#| label: completed-onelead-registered-contrasts
pairs = [
    ("wavelet increment", "A0_raw", "A0_wave_noSSL_gated_add"),
    ("SSL increment", "A0_wave_noSSL_gated_add", "ssl_magnitude_phase_local_gated_add"),
    ("physiological view", "R0_morlet_mag_morlet_phase", "R1_morlet_mag_ueg_phase"),
    ("E1 complementarity", "ssl_magnitude_phase_local_gated_add", "E1_ssl_local"),
]
rows = []
keys = ["seed", "observed_lead"]
for label, left_name, right_name in pairs:
    left = completed.loc[completed.cell_name.eq(left_name), keys + metrics]
    right = completed.loc[completed.cell_name.eq(right_name), keys + metrics]
    for _, row in left.merge(right, on=keys, suffixes=("_left", "_right")).iterrows():
        out = {"contrast": label, "left": left_name, "right": right_name,
               "seed": row.seed, "observed_lead": row.observed_lead}
        for metric in metrics:
            sign = -1 if metric_direction(metric) == "min" else 1
            out[f"improvement.{metric}"] = sign * (row[f"{metric}_right"] - row[f"{metric}_left"])
        rows.append(out)
display(pd.DataFrame(rows) if rows else pd.DataFrame([{"status": "contrast unavailable"}]))
```

These contrasts isolate reviewer-relevant questions, but the experiment has one
seed. They nominate configurations for convergence testing; they do not supply
uncertainty estimates or multiplicity-controlled confirmation.

## What the registered contrasts actually show

The wavelet increment is the clearest short-screen effect. Relative to A0 raw,
the wavelet branch without SSL increases wave mIoU by 0.079 on lead I and 0.043
on lead II, boundary F1 by 0.060 and 0.016, and P-wave IoU by 0.171 and 0.083.
QRS IoU changes by only 0.001–0.003. This concentration on P/T rather than QRS
is mechanistically plausible, but it is still an internal three-epoch result.
The branch costs approximately 4.16 GB additional peak GPU memory.

The SSL increment is heterogeneous. On lead I it changes mean Pearson by
−0.0005, lower-tail Pearson by −0.0041, and boundary F1 by −0.0011. On lead II
it changes those endpoints by +0.0030, +0.0040, and +0.0358. It also adds about
8.45 GB beyond the wavelet-only model. The correct screen-level conclusion is
therefore **possible lead-II delineation complementarity**, not a general SSL
improvement.

Replacing Morlet phase with UEG phase changes mean Pearson by less than 0.0002
on either lead. Boundary F1 increases by 0.0030 on lead I and 0.0105 on lead II,
but the lower-tail Pearson direction reverses between leads. This is too small
and inconsistent for a physiology claim without longer matched training.

Only the lead-II E1 complementarity cell completed. It is essentially tied with
A0+wavelet+SSL while using approximately 5.94 GB more memory. Because lead I is
missing, this contrast is both single-seed and asymmetrically censored.

## Endpoint coupling and search multiplicity

```{python}
#| label: completed-onelead-endpoint-coupling
focus_metrics = [c for c in ["metric.val_missing_pearson",
                              "metric.val_missing_pearson_p05",
                              "metric.val_recon_loss", "metric.miou_wave",
                              "metric.boundary_f1_smoke", "metric.P_iou",
                              "metric.QRS_iou", "metric.T_iou"] if c in completed]
correlations = completed[focus_metrics].corr(method="spearman")
display(correlations)
fig = px.imshow(correlations, text_auto=".2f", zmin=-1, zmax=1,
                color_continuous_scale="RdBu", color_continuous_midpoint=0,
                title="Spearman coupling among screening endpoints")
fig.show()

ranked = []
for lead, group in completed.groupby("observed_lead"):
    for metric in focus_metrics:
        ascending = metric_direction(metric) == "min"
        top = group.sort_values(metric, ascending=ascending).iloc[0]
        ranked.append({"observed_lead": lead, "metric": metric,
                       "leader": top.id, "value": top[metric]})
display(pd.DataFrame(ranked))
```

Mean Pearson and reconstruction loss are almost redundant in rank
(absolute Spearman approximately 0.99), while boundary F1 correlates only about
0.11 with mean Pearson. Wave mIoU is moderately coupled to both. This explains
why a reconstruction leader need not be a boundary leader and why a single
composite score embeds a scientific value judgement.

With 115 completed rows and many endpoints, the metric-wise maximum is strongly
subject to winner's curse. A configuration appearing once at the top is a
candidate, not a confirmed effect. The registered contrasts above are more
interpretable than post-hoc leaderboard mining, even though they still lack
replication.

## Screening claim ledger

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A wavelet branch improves short-run delineation | Supported descriptively | Large matched P/T, mIoU, and boundary gains on both leads. |
| The gain is uniform across waves | Contradicted | QRS is nearly unchanged; P and T drive the improvement. |
| SSL generally improves the wavelet model | Not supported | Lead I is tied/slightly worse; lead II improves. |
| UEG phase is superior to Morlet phase | Unresolved | Small effects with lead-dependent directions. |
| E1 is an improved base | Not supported | Only lead II completed and is effectively tied at substantially higher memory. |
| The screen identifies the final best model | Not established | Single seed, three epochs, many comparisons, composite checkpoint selection, and internal smoke delineation. |
